#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 20 -c 1 -t 24h --job-name=SM_HSP_dimer_prod --output=job.{{id}}.out --error=job.{{id}}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from -n 20 with no multi-node specification)
# -n 20        : 20 tasks (from -n 20)
# -c 1         : 1 core per task (from -c 1)
# -t 24h       : 24 hour walltime (from -t 24:00:00)
# --job-name=SM_HSP_dimer_prod : job name (from -J SM_HSP_dimer_prod)
# --output=job.{{id}}.out : output file with job ID (from --output=job.%j.out)
# --error=job.{{id}}.err : error file with job ID (from --error=job.%j.err)
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID instead of %j

# Original Slurm account: youraccount
# Slurm: -A youraccount
# Note: Flux uses different account/bank management through flux-accounting
# If flux-accounting is configured, add to submission command:
# flux batch --setattr=bank=youraccount ...
# Performance impact: Without account specification, job may run under default account
# which could affect priority or resource limits

# Original Slurm job name: SM_HSP_dimer_prod
# Flux: --job-name=SM_HSP_dimer_prod (specified in submission command)

# Original Slurm output/error files
# Flux: --output and --error (specified in submission command)
# Flux uses {{id}} instead of %j for job ID

# Original Slurm time: 24:00:00 (24 hours)
# Flux: -t 24h or -t 1440m or -t 86400s

# Original Slurm cores: -n 20 (tasks) and -c 1 (threads per task)
# Flux: -n 20 -c 1
# This allocates 20 tasks with 1 core each (total 20 cores)

# Module loading
ml purge
ml ABINIT/8.10.3 Armadillo/9.700.2 CDO/1.9.5 GOTM/5.3-221-gac7ec88d NCO/4.8.1 NCO/4.9.2 OpenFOAM/6 OpenFOAM/7 OpenFOAM/v1912 Rosetta/3.7 Siesta/4.1-MaX-1.0 Siesta/4.1-b4 Singular/4.1.2 XCrySDen/1.5.60 XCrySDen/1.6.2 deal.II/9.1.1-gcc deal.II/9.1.1-intel

ml gromacs/2019.6.th

# GROMACS preprocessing
gmx grompp -f md.mdp -c npt.gro -t npt.cpt -p topol.top -o md_0_1.tpr

# GROMACS MD run
# Note: gmx mdrun with -nt 20 will use 20 threads
# This should match the allocated cores (20 cores from -n 20 -c 1)
gmx mdrun -nt 20 -deffnm md_0_1

# Complete submission command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 20 -c 1 -t 24h \
#   --job-name=SM_HSP_dimer_prod \
#   --output=job.{{id}}.out \
#   --error=job.{{id}}.err \
#   script.sh
#
# If account/bank is configured:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 20 -c 1 -t 24h \
#   --job-name=SM_HSP_dimer_prod \
#   --output=job.{{id}}.out \
#   --error=job.{{id}}.err \
#   --setattr=bank=youraccount \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.
Resource allocation is consistent: 20 tasks × 1 core per task = 20 cores total, which matches the gmx mdrun -nt 20 threading specification.
The output/error file placeholders use {{id}} which is correct for Flux, but should be verified against the specific Flux version being used (some versions may use {{jobid}} or other variants).

The script loads an unusually large number of modules (18 modules) including multiple versions of the same software (e.g., NCO/4.8.1 and NCO/4.9.2, OpenFOAM/6, /7, and /v1912). This could lead to module conflicts or environment issues. Consider loading only the modules actually needed for GROMACS.

No memory specification is provided. GROMACS MD simulations can be memory-intensive, and explicit memory allocation might be beneficial. Consider adding memory specifications to the submission command if needed.
The 24-hour walltime is quite long. Verify this is within the cluster's maximum walltime limits.
The account placeholder 'youraccount' should be replaced with an actual account name before submission if flux-accounting is in use.
No validation that input files (md.mdp, npt.gro, npt.cpt, topol.top) exist before running gmx grompp.
No error checking after gmx grompp before proceeding to gmx mdrun. If preprocessing fails, the MD run will also fail.

#!/bin/bash
#project name
#SBATCH -A youraccount
#specify job name
#SBATCH -J SM_HSP_dimer_prod
#set places for error and output files
#SBATCH --error=job.%j.err
#SBATCH --output=job.%j.out
#request a certain number of hours for the run HR:MIN:SEC
#SBATCH -t 24:00:00
# specify number of cores you want
#SBATCH -n 20
# specify number of threads per task
#SBATCH -c 1

# It is always best to do a ml purge before loading modules in a submit file
ml purge
ml ABINIT/8.10.3 Armadillo/9.700.2 CDO/1.9.5 GOTM/5.3-221-gac7ec88d NCO/4.8.1 NCO/4.9.2 OpenFOAM/6 OpenFOAM/7 OpenFOAM/v1912 Rosetta/3.7 Siesta/4.1-MaX-1.0 Siesta/4.1-b4 Singular/4.1.2 XCrySDen/1.5.60 XCrySDen/1.6.2 deal.II/9.1.1-gcc deal.II/9.1.1-intel
